negotiation_details: Customer asks: minimum sustained throughput of 150k tokens/sec during sale windows (30 min windows), p99 latency < 350ms for <=512 token responses.

Redwood proposal: 160k sustained tokens/sec guaranteed across reserved pool (8 A100-eq) with concurrency cap 600 concurrent model sessions; burst to 1,200 concurrency for 90s using token-bucket credit system.
Penalty model on table: service credit tiers tied to % reduction of min_tokens_sec over monthly measured windows; customer requests monetary rebate instead of service credits — legal escalation.
Overage & burst billing: bursts above guaranteed allocation billed as metered usage at negotiated rate; customer prefers capped burst cost (monthly cap) — commercial tradeoffs being discussed.

Routing/fallback: Redwood suggests automatic fallback to slightly lower-cost quantized model variant when sustained throughput > guaranteed for more than 5 minutes; customer wants explicit control for personalization fidelity.
Monitoring: Redwood to expose token/sec, concurrency, p50/p95/p99 latency per route and alerting thresholds. Customer requires audit logs for 12 months (data residency note).
technical_requirements: VPC peering w/ private IP ranges, strict egress controls.
Pinned model versions for production personalization pipelines; rollback policy required.
KV/prefix caching recommended for repeated prompt prefixes to reduce per-token load.
Target latency: p95 < 250ms for 128-token responses; p99 < 350ms for <=512 tokens during guaranteed windows.
Autoscaling guardrails: no automatic scale-down below reserved baseline during guaranteed hours.
commercial_terms_under_discussion: Reserved capacity: 8x A100-eq GPUs, 12-month commitment, option to increase to 12 GPUs at fixed uplift.
Throughput guarantee: min_tokens_sec = 160,000 across cluster during defined 'peak windows' (customer to provide schedule).
Concurrency cap: default 600 concurrent requests, burst to 1,200 for up to 90s using token-bucket; overflow handled by queueing with 503 after soft limit.
SLA remediation: customer requests direct rebates for missed min_tokens_sec (sliding scale); Redwood prefers predefined service credit table — legal to reconcile.
Security add-ons: extended audit log retention and HSM/KMS integration priced as add-on.
